newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-PORTRAITS OF AUSTRALIA'S ASHES SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PORTRAITS OF AUSTRALIA'S ASHES SQUAD.

text.p: Following are brief player biographies of Australia's squad for the six-test Ashes tour of England starting next month.

MICHAEL BEVAN (8/5/70) Left-handed batsman, left-arm wrist-spinner. A revelation as a bowler in partnership with leg-spinner Shane Warne in the home series against West Indies during the southern hemisphere summer, Bevan has yet to fully convince as a top order batsman.
Test matches: 14. Innings: 24. Average: 34.76. Highest score: 91 v Pakistan, Lahore, 1994-95. Wickets: 25. Average: 20.32. Best bowling: 6/82 v West Indies, Adelaide 1996-97. State: New South Wales.

ANDREW BICHEL (27/8/70). Right-arm fast-medium bowler. Bichel proved a capable new ball bowler against West Indies but struggled to make an impact during the tour to South Africa. Appears to have slipped behind Jason Gillespie as a potential strike partner with Glenn McGrath.
2. 3. 13.33. 18 v West Indies, Perth, 1996-97. 1. 143.00. 1/31 v West Indies, Adelaide 1996-97. State: Queensland.

GREG BLEWETT (29/10/71). Right-handed batsman, right-arm medium pace bowler. A stylish batsman with a wide range of shots, Blewett has thrived as both an opener and number three batsman for South Australia. Cemented his test place in Australia's middle order with a double century in the first test against South Africa. Some critics cite supposed technical deficiences in defence. Began his test career with centuries in successive tests against England in 1994-95.
16. 27. 41.60. 214 v South Africa, Johannesburg, 1996-97. 4. 65.00. 2/25 v Pakistan, Hobart 1995-96. State: South Australia.

MATTHEW ELLIOTT (28/9/71). Left-handed batsman. Elliott broke into the test ranks against West Indies last season but his initial term ended prematurely when he badly injured his knee in a mid-wicket collision with teammate Mark Waugh. A sound technician, he returned for the tour to South Africa but failed to convince fully after being switched to number three in the order.
5. 9. 38.75. 85 v South Africa, Johannesburg, 1996-97. State: Victoria.

ADAM GILCHRIST (14/11/71). Left-handed batsman, wicket-keeper. Regarded as a genuine top order batsman, Gilchrist has long been touted as a future successor for Ian Healy behind the stumps. Gilchrist played against South Africa in a limited overs international as a batsman.
Gilchrist has not played test cricket. State: Western Australia.

JASON GILLESPIE (19/4/75). Right-arm fast bowler. The highest wicket-taker on either side in South Africa with 14 wickets in three tests at an average of 20, Gillespie emerged as Glenn McGrath's new-ball partner, moving ahead of Andy Bichel in the pecking order. Quick, enthusiastic and tireless worker, but lacking experience at test level. At 21, his best years surely remain ahead of him.
5. 7. 14.50. 16 not out v West Indies, Sydney, 1996-97. 16. 23.81. 5/54 v South Africa, Port Elizabeth 1996-97. State: South Australia.

IAN HEALY (30/4/64). Right-handed batsman, wicket-keeper. Ever-reliable with the gloves, Healy lost the vice-captaincy to all-rounder Steve Waugh. Healy has gradually improved as a batsman, a development highlighted by his fine century in the first test against West Indies last season. Took over as captain in the limited overs series against South Africa after Mark Taylor stood down. A fierce competitor, Healy's temperament came under question with his suspension in South Africa for dissent. Only the second Australian after Rodney Marsh to take more than 300 test dismissals.
88. 133. 28.22. 161 not out v West Indies, Brisbane, 1996-97. Catches: 282. Stumpings: 20. State: Queensland.

BRENDON JULIAN (10/8/70). Right-handed batsman, left-arm fast-medium pace bowler. The lanky paceman was recalled for the limited overs series against South Africa after several years out of the limelight. Helped Western Australia reach the domestic Sheffield Shield final. An Ashes tourist to England four years ago.
7. 9. 16.00. 56 not out v England, Nottingham 1993. 15. 39.93. 4/36 v West Indies, Bridgetown, 1994-95. State: Western Australia

MICHAEL KASPROWICZ (10/2/72). Right-arm fast bowler. The leading wicket-taker in the domestic Sheffield Shield with 48 wickets at an average of 25.54, helping Queensland to the title. Kasprowicz endured a frustrating test baptism when he failed to take a wicket in the first two tests against West Indies last season before being dropped. Has experience of English conditions after playing for Essex in 1994, taking 60 first-class wickets.
2. 2. 13.5. 21 v West Indies, Sydney, 1996-97. 0. State: Queensland.

JUSTIN LANGER (21/11/70). Left-handed batsman. Brought up on the quick pitches of the WACA ground in Perth, Langer is a fine player of fast bowling, as he showed during his test debut series against West Indies in 1992-93. Strong off the back foot, but may find English seaming pitches pose fresh problems.
8. 12. 22.66. 69 v Pakistan, Lahore, 1994-95. State: Western Australia.

GLENN MCGRATH (9/2/70). Right-arm fast bowler. With the retirement of veteran Craig McDermott last season, McGrath has emerged as Australia's strike fast bowler. Led the attack superbly against West Indies and South Africa, prompting captain Mark Taylor to describe the lanky bowler as the best in his trade in the world. His form with the ball is expected to be a vital factor in Australia's bid to retain the Ashes.
28. 32. 3.24. Highest score: 24 v West Indies, Sydney, 1996-97. 119. 24.66. 6/47 v West Indies, Port-of-Spain, 1994-95. State: New South Wales.

RICKY PONTING (19/12/74). Right-handed batsman, right-arm medium pace. Unceremoniously dumped during the test series against West Indies and overlooked for the tour to South Africa, Ponting persuaded selectors he was worth a recall with a string of centuries in the domestic Sheffield Shield. Highly-rated as an aggressive, fluent batsman and a potential long-term candidate for the troublesome number three spot in the order.
6. 10. 33.00. Highest score: 96 v Sri Lanka, Perth, 1995-96. 2. 4.00. 1/0 v West Indies, Brisbane, 1996-97. State: Tasmania.

MICHAEL SLATER (21/2/70). Right-handed batsman, right-arm medium pace. An outstanding success on the last Ashes tour, Slater appeared destined for a long test career after his double century against Sri Lanka in 1995-96. But despite a high test average, selectors lost patience with the New South Wales opener after an indifferent spell and left him out against West Indies. At his best, Slater is capable of destroying the best bowling attacks but also prone to rash shot-selection.
34. 59. 47.41. 219 v Sri Lanka, Perth, 1995-96. 1. 4.00. 1/4 v Pakistan, Rawalpindi, 1994-95. State: New South Wales.

MARK TAYLOR (27/10/64). Left-handed batsman, right-arm bowler. Widely acclaimed for his leadership and tactical abilities, Taylor has survived as Australia captain despite a dismal slump in form. The burly opener has not scored a test 50 since late 1995. Dropped himself from the Australian side during the recent limited overs series against South Africa. Led Australia to Ashes win at home two years ago. A niggling back injury adds to his current troubles.
81. 145. 42.64. 219 v England, Nottingham, 1989. 1. 26.00. 1/11 v Pakistan, Rawalpindi, 1994-95. State: New South Wales.

SHANE WARNE (13/9/69). Right-handed batsman, right-arm leg-spin bowler. Long regarded as the world's finest spinner since making his test debut against India in 1991-92. Warne proved a revelation on the last Ashes tour four years ago but has struggled to assert himself in similar fashion since undergoing finger surgery last year. Has gone 13 test matches without taking five wickets in an innings but he and McGrath are Australia's key weapons against England.
52. 70. 13.75. 74 not out v New Zealand, Brisbane, 1993-94. 240. 23.94. 8/71 v England, Brisbane, 1994-95. State: Victoria.

MARK WAUGH (2/6/65). Right-handed batsman, right-arm medium bowler. A stylish, fluent strokemaker, Waugh is unchallenged as Australia's number four batsman. His century in the second test against South Africa in Port Elizabeth was a turning point in the series. Waugh has converted himself from a medium-pacer to off-spinner with some success in recent years. A natural sportsman and a brilliant and agile fieldsman at second slip.
63. 102. 43.42. 140 v England, Brisbane, 1994-95. 40. 36.83. 5/40 v England, Adelaide, 1994-95. State: New South Wales.

STEPHEN WAUGH (2/6/65). Right-handed batsman, right-arm medium bowler. Promoted to vice-captain for the Ashes tour. Batting at number five, Waugh acts as a resolute foil to his twin brother, Mark. Once regarded as a genuine all-rounder, a succession of injuries have forced Waugh, Australia's senior test cricketer, to concentrate increasingly on his batting. Player of the series against South Africa. One of the few current players to average more than 50 in test cricket.
89. 138. 50.64. 200 v West Indies, Kingston, 1994-95. 80. 35.23. 5/28 v South Africa, Cape Town, 1993-94. State: New South Wales.
